content: Sotagliflozin is a dual inhibitor of sodium-glucose cotransporter 1 (SGLT1) and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2). It has recently been approved by the FDA to reduce the risks of cardiovascular death, hospitalization for heart failure, and urgent visits related to heart failure in patients with type 2 diabetes, chronic kidney disease (CKD), or other cardiovascular risk factors. Unlike other SGLT2 inhibitors, sotagliflozin also inhibits SGLT1, which delays glucose absorption in the intestine. This dual mechanism provides more comprehensive glycemic control and makes it effective in addressing both type 1 and type 2 diabetes. In the SCORED and SOLOIST-WHF clinical trials, sotagliflozin demonstrated significant benefits in reducing cardiovascular events and hospitalizations. Specifically, the primary composite outcome included reductions in cardiovascular death, heart failure events, and urgent heart failure-related hospitalizations. In the SOLOIST-WHF trial, participants with worsening heart failure were randomized to receive either sotagliflozin or a placebo. Those treated with sotagliflozin showed a significantly lower rate of urgent heart failure visits compared to the placebo group. However, gastrointestinal side effects, such as diarrhea, were more frequently observed in patients taking sotagliflozin compared to other SGLT2 inhibitors. This is attributed to SGLT1 inhibition, which increases sugar levels in the gut and affects the gastrointestinal system. While sotagliflozin effectively reduced cardiovascular morbidity, no statistically significant reduction in all-cause mortality was observed in the trials.
